decisive_items: pedunculated bony protrusion arising from the posterolateral plantar aspect of the calcaneus
Magnetic resonance imaging of the left foot showed no thickening of the plantar fascia
The gastrocnemius remained tight with a positive Silfverskiöld test
response.rationale: MRI reveals a pedunculated calcaneal bony protrusion, pathognomonic for Haglund syndrome, while plantar fasciitis is excluded by normal MRI findings and gastrocnemius tightness is a secondary feature.

rejected.why: MRI showed no plantar fascia thickening, contradicting plantar fasciitis despite tenderness.
Gastrocnemius tightness is present but not the underlying cause; the bony protrusion is the key finding.
